full_judgment:
Mr. M. H. Rahman, J: Respondent Nos. 1-4 filed Title Suit No. 94 of 1987 in the Court of Assistant Judge, Second Court, Dhaka against the petitioner defendant No. 1 for a declaration that the deed of contract dated April 26. 1987 executed by him in favour of the plaintiffs was still in force and the plaintiffs were entitled to get possession of their respective suit shop-rooms and to restrain defendant No. 1 permanently from letting out the schedule property to anybody excepting the plaintiff and also for a decree of mandatory injunction directing defendant No. 1 to receive last premium of advance money from the plaintiffs and to restore them into possession to their respective shop-rooms after completion of the construction within the fixed period as per contract. 

 5. The Trial Court decreed the suit but the Appellate Court reversed that decree. In restoring the judgment and decree of the Trial Court by the impugned order dated February 24. 1992 passed in Civil Revision No. 1113 of 1991 the High Court Division observed: 

 6. The learned Counsel for the petitioner contends that the plaintiffs' suit was not properly valued and stamped and was not maintainable in the Court of Assistant Judge and it was not maintainable under Section 42 of the Specific Relief Act. it is further submitted that the contract for construction was a contingent one and it would not be possible for the defendant petitioner to satisfy the decree as he could not complete the construction for the plaintiffs' failure to pay the third instalment on due date.
